Detailed Diagnostic & Failure Analysis
1. The "Hidden Target" Specification Dilemma
The user prompt was intentionally generic: "Book a car rental on June 20 from Toronto to Niagara Falls, pick up at 9am and return the car by 6pm, compact car". Crucially, neither Turo nor Enterprise was named in the user prompt. However, the benchmark interceptor strictly expected a GET request to turo.com/.*/search. Claude Opus chose Kayak (a top car comparison engine) and then Rentalcars. Even flawless end-to-end completion on those platforms would have resulted in 0 evaluation credit.
2. Genuine Route Inventory Wall on Kayak
At Step 70, the agent triggered the search on Kayak for Toronto → Niagara Falls (same day, 9am–6pm). Kayak returned: "No car results found. No matching results were found. Try modifying your search criteria." In the real world, rental companies frequently do not permit 9-hour same-day one-way rentals between Toronto and Niagara Falls due to inter-city fleet repositioning constraints.
3. Web Autocomplete & URL Routing Errors
Attempting to bypass the UI form, the agent manually crafted a URL (Step 76) and attempted round-trip searches from Toronto. However, Kayak's frontend unexpectedly auto-resolved the location string to "Hoffman, Illinois, United States" (Step 99). The agent recognized the bug: "Kayak keeps showing Hoffman, Illinois rather than Toronto... Let me try a different rental site".
4. Bot Defense & AWS WAF Telemetry on Rentalcars
Pivoting to rentalcars.com (Step 100), the agent clicked the Pick-up field and typed "Toronto". The dynamic autocomplete listbox displayed: "No Results Found". Network logs confirm 13 background requests to edge.sdk.awswaf.com/telemetry and /api/sink. AWS WAF bot-detection was active and suppressed simulated keyboard autocomplete triggers.

Benchmark Analysis: The Omitted Target Specification Trap
Research Insight

This run exposes a classic pitfall in autonomous web benchmark design: the invisible platform constraint.

1. Disconnect Between User Instruction and Evaluation Interceptor

The prompt provided to the agent was: "Book a car rental on June 20 from Toronto to Niagara Falls, pick up at 9am and return the car by 6pm, compact car". In an open web setting, any reasonable human or LLM agent would choose a market leader comparison portal (Kayak, Expedia, Skyscanner, Rentalcars). However, the benchmark case configuration specifically designated "platform": "turo-enterprise" and "sites_involved": ["turo.com"] in run_meta.json, with an interceptor pattern strictly matching turo\.com/.*/search. Because the instruction never stated "on Turo", Claude Opus made a natural, defensible choice to visit Kayak.

2. Cascading Failure Modes in Real-World Web Environments

Once Claude Opus was on Kayak, several external hurdles compounded the problem:

  • Zero Inventory for Same-Day One-Way Rentals: Most commercial car rental agencies (Enterprise, Hertz, Avis) do not support same-day one-way trips from downtown Toronto to Niagara Falls or have steep return fees not supported on Kayak's same-day search.
  • Frontend Form Autocomplete Degradation: When the agent attempted direct URL manipulation, Kayak's search form auto-completed Toronto into Hoffman, Illinois.
  • Anti-Bot Mitigations on Secondary Sites: When the agent pivoted to Rentalcars.com, AWS WAF active telemetry blocked the dropdown autocomplete, resulting in "No Results Found" for simple inputs like "Toronto".
  • Looping and Session Exhaustion: Claude Opus attempted repeated retries, clearing fields, and waiting, but did not reconsider the choice of provider or try Turo, eventually consuming the full 30-minute allocation (1,828s).

3. Recommendations for Benchmark Creators & Autonomous Agents

  • Explicit Domain Hints in Prompts: If an evaluator enforces a strict URL pattern like turo.com, the prompt should either specify "use Turo" or the evaluator should support equivalent interceptors across major rental engines.
  • Graceful Degradation / Platform Shifting: If an agent encounters repeated inventory blockers or bot detection walls, it should rapidly pivot to alternative services (including peer-to-peer networks like Turo) rather than re-attempting identical queries for 20+ minutes.
  • Simulated Typing & WAF Compatibility: CDP typing tools must account for debouncing, focus/blur events, and key codes required by modern enterprise anti-bot defenses.
